interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Twenty tenths equals how many sevenths?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

Use the seven equal intervals in each unit and count the intervals from zero to the target point.
The target is two complete units, and each unit is divided into seven sevenths. Count two groups of seven intervals.
Starting at zero, move seven sevenths to reach one unit and seven more sevenths to reach the target point.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many sevenths are needed to reach the same point as 20/10.
Multiply the whole-number value shown by Line 1 by the target denominator.
Use the value 2 from Line 1 and the denominator 7 from Line 2 to form the numerator.
Calculate two groups of seven by adding seven to itself twice, then enter that product in R1_user.

misconceptions.description: Aluno mantém o numerador original (20) e apenas altera o denominador, sem entender a equivalência
misconceptions.feedback: You kept the original numerator even though the denominator changed. Count the sevenths needed to represent the same two units.

misconceptions.description: Aluno inverte a fração equivalente encontrada
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the denominator as the numerator. The field asks only for the numerator, while 7 is already displayed as the denominator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno tenta manter a 'distância' entre os termos da fração original
misconceptions.feedback: You preserved the difference between the original numerator and denominator. Equivalent fractions are found by matching the value, not by preserving that difference.

hints.message: Compare the positions marked on the two number lines rather than comparing the numerators alone.
Use the comparison selector to show whether the two fractions have equal or different values.
The marked points reach the same location, so choose the symbol used when two quantities have the same value.
Select the middle comparison symbol for sameness, then press Done to complete the exercise.
